GAME TIME

Basketball School

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

2-ON-2 AROUND THE CONE

IG MIN BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 cone and 1 ball per half-court

### DESCRIPTION

An offense and a defense will start underneath the rim facing the half-court line, with the offense first and in possession of the ball, and the defender standing behind. Another offensive player will stand in the right corner, with a help defender positioned appropriately. Offense can start at any moment by dribbling around the cone on the left wing. The defender must trail, creating an advantage situation for a live 2-on-2.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Driving and kicking decision-making
- Converting advantages
- Defense recovering back to neutral

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add a second cone three big steps behind the first cone. The defense must run around the second cone, while the offense dribbles around the first. This increases the advantage.
- Change the location of the second offensive players every repetition.
- Have players complete three repetitions in a row before changing roles.
- Add an extra offensive and defensive player so it is 3-on-3.
- Add an extra cone, players can choose what side they dribble to. Other offensive players must start in 'bad spacing' and find a good spacing location to re-space to as the dribble starts.

### STAFF ROLE

- Place the cones on the wing.
- Encourage quick rotations to save time.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "When is a good time to pass the ball to your teammate?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-2 CONVERSION INTO 2-ON-1 BACK

12 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided into groups of three. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. One player will start on the baseline with a ball facing half-court. One defender will guard the ball-handler from the baseline to the free-throw line, and another defender will play defense between the free-throw line and half-court line. The offensive player must attempt to dribble to the half-court line to score a 'touchdown' within 10 seconds, without losing possession of the ball. The defenders can only stay in their areas. If the offense scores a 'touchdown' or the defense forces a turnover (steal, out of bounds, time limit), it changes to a 2-on-1 at the same basket (with offense and the defense switching roles). Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.

### SCORING

The ball-handler will get 3 points for successfully completing a touchdown. In the 2-on-1, the offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Handling pressure
- Disruptive defense

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders can only use one hand to defend.
- Remove the first defender's space limitations while keeping the second defender's limitations.
- Add another offensive player so that it is 2-on-2.
- Add in the 'rugby' load where offensive players can only pass laterally or backwards.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the space?"
- "What is the best shot to obtain within the 2-on-1?"

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players stay in their respective areas.
- Count down from 10 seconds.

I-ON-I-I CREATE SEPARATION

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of three. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. One player will start on offense, one on defense, and one as the 'facilitator.' The facilitator's job is to help the offense to score. The offensive player can pass to them and receive the ball back, as well as use the facilitator to screen for them. The offense has three dribbles on every catch to score. The facilitator can move around freely, and the offensive player should start in different locations. Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defender must play defense with one hand behind their back
- Players receive a bonus point for scoring inside the charge circle
- Players have no dribbles

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.
- Help the facilitator be proactive in creating an advantage for the offensive player.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

CE

### CUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could you help your teammate to score?"
- "Defensively, how could you disrupt your opponent to make it more challenging?"

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Facilitator exploring ways to create advantages
- Disruptive defense
- Creative finishing

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 SCRAMBLE

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will start in different spacings outside the 3PT line and three defenders will begin anywhere inside the paint. The defense will start with the ball and pass to any offensive player. From here, a live 3-on-3 begins. The defense must scramble and attempt to recover back to neutral to cancel the advantage. Games will last until a basket is made or there is a defensive stop (defensive rebound or forced turnover). Repeat for three repetitions before the offense and defense switch roles.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Remove one defender and play 3-on-2 if too difficult for the offense.
- A coach throws the pass in instead of the defense, making the scramble more unpredictable. This means the defense must communicate to confirm who is covering the ball as they closeout.
- Offense plays from a different spacing each time.
- The offense must dribble/sprint to the half-court line while the defense must touch the sideline in order to transition in between repetitions.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Make sure the defense starts inside the paint.
- Remind defenders to call 'ball' on closeouts.
- Help with the dynamic start load to transition between repetitions.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Scrambling and locating match-ups
- Defense recovering back to neutral

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can we closeout to prevent a wide open shot?"
- "How can the offense keep their advantage?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 THREE TRIPS

18 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available full-court spaces

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per full-court

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided up into teams of three. Ideally, there will be a maximum of five teams per basket. If there are high numbers, use the same activity but 4-on-4 or 5-on-5. Players will begin lining up to shoot a free-throw. As soon as the free-throw is shot, a live 3-on-3 is played. If the offense secures an offensive rebound, they may immediately look to score again. If the defense secures the ball, they look to transition to the other end to begin the first 'trip.' Three trips are played, with the activity stopping after the third trip is completed.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating spacing and advantage
- Transitioning on offense and defense

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line). Players must space outside the 3PT line during the transition trips.
- Outlet passes off a rebound are a turnover. Instead, whoever rebounds the ball must push the ball to start transition with greater pace.
- Scores within six seconds of gaining possession are worth double.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players with the free-throw line-up if needed.
- Encourage players to maintain effective spacing and to transition running wide and fast.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could we transition faster?"
- "Defensively, how should we transition back to reduce fast break opportunities?"
